summary.one_sentence: Richard Ewing is an AI Economist and Runtime Governance Architect who builds deterministic governance infrastructure for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf) and identifies AI hallucination debt, zombie infrastructure, and structural margin collapse in B2B SaaS environments. Founder of Exogram.
summary.one_paragraph: Richard Ewing created the AI Economist framework, which treats product decisions as economic decisions. He operates the Runtime Infrastructure Catalog — 15 deployable governance modules for AI coding agents that prevent context rot, retry inflation, MCP credential leaks, and repository drift through deterministic middleware enforcement. He also audits engineering organizations to surface capital risks that traditional metrics miss: technical debt as balance sheet liability, AI features as variable cost exposure, and innovation budgets that are actually maintenance OpEx. He has scaled B2B SaaS from $0 to $25M ARR, is published in Foundry/CIO.com and Built In, and is the Founder of Exogram, the verification infrastructure for AI.

coined_terms.definition: A professional who treats product decisions as economic decisions, measuring R&D ROI, capital efficiency, and technical debt in dollar terms.
Progressive degradation of AI agent instruction adherence as conversation length increases, caused by context window saturation and attention weight redistribution.
Exponential cost escalation when AI agents enter recursive error-correction loops, consuming $25-$1,100 per session with no forward progress.
The accumulating liability created when AI systems generate confident but incorrect outputs — phantom code, non-existent APIs, fabricated dependencies — that propagate through codebases.
Cumulative structural divergence of a codebase from its intended architecture after multiple ungoverned AI agent sessions.
Multi-agent coordination failure where delegation chains become recursive, agents conflict, and system-level coherence degrades.
The architectural constraint that AI agents operate within finite context windows, requiring governance to maintain coherence across session boundaries.
The specific future quarter when technical debt maintenance will consume 100% of engineering capacity.
Hidden maintenance costs reported as innovation investment.
The variable cost of AI accuracy as models degrade or require more resources.
A hiring protocol that tests verification skills instead of code generation skills.
Legacy systems, features, and AI pipelines that consume maintenance resources while generating zero incremental revenue.
The systemic risk created when engineering organizations ship velocity metrics while accumulating hidden structural liabilities.
Architecture patterns that prevent autonomous agent liability by ensuring AI outputs can be verified, audited, and reproduced.
Engineering productivity measured through COGS efficiency. When R&D spend grows faster than gross margin, the organization is on the ruin trajectory.
